acceptance: A code change that alters any committed bundle's class fails a required check that names the bundles.
context:
Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).

2026-11-20 design written, awaiting the owner's choice (none made). Facts at develop 9703d6d98c: 500 bundles; 72 record a class (24 official, 26 unofficial_nonstandard, 22 unofficial_subscale); 38 have an effective class that differs from the record (13 ClickBench, 25 TPC-H subscale). Flipping one scale's list membership would change the class of 474 bundles; removing TPC-DS SF 10 moves 5 official bundles to unofficial_nonstandard and validate_corpus.py still exits 0. No committed bundle is at TPC-DS 10000 or above. Correction to this item: the bundle validator has its own copy of the scale test (_is_nonstandard_scale) and does not call subscale_policy; the Explorer transformer (_compliance_class, _power_score) and submit_classification also classify from the current registry and were not listed. Options: (1) look up the scale list by the bundle's production version or date (7 TPC-DS-OBT bundles change class if keyed on version; needs a list history; does not catch code-rule changes); (2) record the class or a standard-scale marker per bundle at acceptance, in the bundle (all 500 hashes change), the sidecar (44 bundles lack one) or one corpus file; (3) snapshot each committed bundle's effective class and fail any change, in corpus-inventory.json (waits on the mirror validator item) or a develop-only file. Open questions for the owner: which option and variant; whether protection also covers code-rule changes (subscale threshold, RANKING_EXCLUDED_COMPLIANCE_CLASSES); whether any reclassification of committed bundles is ever legitimate and by what mechanism.

Owner decision 2026-11-20. Question: a registry edit silently reclassifies stored bundles. Answer: "Recommended: the smallest fix. A committed snapshot of every bundle's class plus a check that fails, naming the bundles, when a code change alters any of them. No bundle or schema change." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20. This is the approved design; the 474-of-500 figure is an earlier reviewer's simulation and is re-measured by the new check, not relied on.

## Guardrails (accepted by the owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, resolves a review thread, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
description:
## Problem
Since #4304 a bundle's effective compliance class is derived at read time from current code (the scale lists and the classification rules). A code change can therefore reclassify stored bundles, including ones stamped official, with corpus validation still passing; #4335 showed this for TPC-DS 10000 and above (latent: the corpus has none).

## Owner decision
Chosen option: "Recommended: the smallest fix. A committed snapshot of every bundle's class plus a check that fails, naming the bundles, when a code change alters any of them. No bundle or schema change." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
Add a committed snapshot file on develop mapping each committed bundle to its effective class, a command that regenerates it, and a check (wired into required CI through the existing corpus checks) that fails and names the bundles when the computed class of any committed bundle differs from the snapshot. A deliberate reclassification is then a visible diff of the snapshot in the same pull request.

## Decision gates
No bundle bytes and no bundle schema change. The snapshot's path and format are stated in the pull request body. This does not wait for the mirror-validator item.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test edits a scale list in memory and the check fails naming the affected bundles; a second test changes a classification rule (the subscale threshold or the ranking-excluded classes) and the check fails; with no change the check passes on the committed corpus; adding a new bundle without updating the snapshot fails with a message that says how to regenerate; corpus validation counts on develop are unchanged.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
